questions.title: Safe Division Checker
questions.description:
Division by zero crashes a program with an ArithmeticException. Read two integers a and b, then print their integer quotient. If b is zero, catch the ArithmeticException and print a friendly error message instead of letting the program crash.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print 'Result: q' where q is a divided by b (integer division). If b is zero, print 'Error: Division by zero'.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000

questions.title: Number Token Parser
questions.description:
User input always arrives as a String until you convert it. Read one token and try to convert it to an int with Integer.parseInt. If the token is not a valid integer, Java raises NumberFormatException; catch it and print a friendly message instead of crashing.

Input Format:
A single line containing one token (letters, digits, or a mix).

Output Format:
Print 'Number: v' when parsing succeeds. Otherwise print 'Invalid number'.

Constraints:
The token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Array Access with Fallback
questions.description:
Reading past the end of an array throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Read n, then n integers into an array, and finally an index. Print the element stored at that index, or catch the exception and print a fallback message.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated integers. Third line: the index to read.

Output Format:
Print 'Value: x' for a valid index. For any out-of-range index (including negative), print 'Error: Index out of range'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100 and each element satisfies -1000 <= x <= 1000. The index can be any integer.

questions.title: Quotient with Finally Cleanup
questions.description:
A finally block runs no matter what happened inside the try. Read two integers a and b and print their quotient inside try, catch a zero divisor in catch, and always print the cleanup line from finally — once on success and once after an error.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
First print 'Quotient: q' (or 'Error: Division by zero' when b is zero). Then always print 'Cleanup done'.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput2:
Error: Division by zero
Cleanup done

questions.title: Two Catch Blocks Selector
questions.description:
One try can be followed by several catch blocks, each handling a different exception type. Read two tokens, convert both to integers, and print their quotient. A non-integer token raises NumberFormatException while a zero divisor raises ArithmeticException — the matching catch block decides the message.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated tokens.

Output Format:
Print 'Quotient: q' on success. Print 'Invalid number' if either token is not an integer, or 'Division by zero' if the divisor is zero.

Constraints:
Each token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Message from the Exception
questions.description:
Every exception object carries a detail message you can read with getMessage(). Read two integers and print their quotient. When the divisor is zero, catch the ArithmeticException and print its message prefixed with 'Caught: '.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
Print 'Quotient: q' on success. If b is zero, print 'Caught: / by zero' (the exception's own message).

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000

questions.title: ATM Withdrawal Guard
questions.description:
An ATM must reject withdrawals that exceed the account balance. Read the balance and the requested amount. If the amount is larger than the balance, use throw to raise new IllegalArgumentException with the message 'Insufficient balance' and catch it in main; otherwise complete the withdrawal.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: balance and amount.

Output Format:
On success print two lines: 'Withdrawn: amount' and 'Remaining balance: newBalance'. If the request is rejected, print exactly one line: 'Transaction failed: Insufficient balance'.

Constraints:
0 <= balance, amount <= 1000000

questions.title: Safe Grade Mapper
questions.description:
A teacher portal converts numeric scores into letter grades, but students sometimes type nonsense like 'abc'. NumberFormatException is an unchecked exception, so the compiler never forces you to handle it — catching it anyway keeps the portal alive. Read one score token and map it: 90 or more prints A, 75 to 89 prints B, 60 to 74 prints C, and anything below 60 prints D.

Input Format:
A single token: a score, or any non-numeric token.

Output Format:
Print 'Grade: X' where X is one of A, B, C, D for a valid integer. Print 'Invalid score' when the token cannot be parsed as an int.

Constraints:
The token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Safe Matrix Cell Reader
questions.description:
A heatmap dashboard reads one requested cell of a matrix. Accessing a row or column outside the matrix throws ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; catch it and report a clear message instead of crashing.

Input Format:
First line: r and c. Next r lines: c space-separated integers each. Last line: i and j, the requested cell.

Output Format:
Print 'Cell: value' for a valid cell. Otherwise print 'Error: Cell out of bounds'.

Constraints:
1 <= r, c <= 20 and each cell value satisfies -100 <= v <= 100.

questions.title: Warehouse Order Validator
questions.description:
A warehouse app refuses orders larger than the available stock. Define a custom unchecked exception class OutOfStockException that extends RuntimeException and stores a message via super(message). When the requested quantity exceeds the stock, throw it from the ordering method; catch it in main and print the rejection.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers: stock and requested.

Output Format:
Print 'Order confirmed: q units' on success. On rejection print 'Order failed: Only s left in stock'.

Constraints:
0 <= stock, requested <= 100000
questions.sampleoutput2: Order failed: Only 3 left in stock
questions.output1: Order failed: Only 0 left in stock

questions.title: Age Validator Checked Exception
questions.description:
Many real-world validations use custom checked exceptions so that callers cannot forget to handle them. Create a class InvalidAgeException that extends Exception and stores a detail message through super(message). Method checkAge(int age) declares 'throws InvalidAgeException' and throws it with message 'Invalid age: age' whenever age is below 18 or above 100. Catch it in main and report the failure using getMessage().

Input Format:
A single line with one integer: age.

Output Format:
Print 'Valid age: age' when 18 <= age <= 100. Otherwise print 'Error: Invalid age: age'.

Constraints:
0 <= age <= 150

questions.title: Finally Always Executes
questions.description:
A processing job must always run its cleanup step, even when an operation blows up midway. Read n, then n pairs of integers, printing 'Result: a/b' (integer division) for each pair. Keep the whole loop inside ONE try block: when a pair has divisor zero the ArithmeticException aborts the remaining pairs, the catch prints 'Error: / by zero', and the finally block still prints the single cleanup line 'Cleanup done' — no matter what happened.

Input Format:
First line: n. Each of the next n lines: two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
'Result: q' for each processed pair. 'Error: / by zero' if a division failed. Exactly one final line 'Cleanup done' in every case.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000 and -1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput2:
Result: 5
Error: / by zero
Cleanup done
questions.output3:
Result: 1
Error: / by zero
Cleanup done

questions.title: Inventory Quantity Guard
questions.description:
Unchecked custom exceptions keep call sites clean because no throws declaration is required. Create a class InvalidQuantityException that extends RuntimeException. The method placeOrder(int quantity) throws it with message 'Invalid quantity: q' when quantity is zero or negative, and otherwise prints the confirmation. Handle the failure in main.

Input Format:
A single line with one integer: quantity.

Output Format:
Print 'Order placed for q units' when quantity >= 1. Otherwise print 'Order rejected: Invalid quantity: q'.

Constraints:
-1000 <= quantity <= 1000

questions.title: Throws Propagation Chain
questions.description:
Instead of catching an exception where it occurs, a method can declare it with throws and let it propagate up the call chain until some caller handles it. Here parse(token) declares NumberFormatException, divide(a, b) declares NumberFormatException and ArithmeticException, and only main catches — one catch of RuntimeException covering both unchecked types. Print the result, or let main report the exception's own message.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated tokens a and b.

Output Format:
Print 'Result: q' when both tokens parse and b is nonzero. Otherwise print 'Handled in main: message' where message is the exception's getMessage() — for example / by zero (zero divisor) or For input string: "abc" (bad token).

Constraints:
Each token has length between 1 and 20.
questions.output1: Handled in main: For input string: "abc"
questions.output3: Handled in main: For input string: "7x"

questions.title: Catch Order Hierarchy
questions.description:
Exception types form a hierarchy, and Java checks catch blocks from top to bottom, using the FIRST compatible one. NumberFormatException is a subclass of IllegalArgumentException, so its catch block must come first — the reverse order would not even compile. Read a type and a value and dispatch: type num parses the value, type arg rejects values shorter than 3 characters by throwing IllegalArgumentException with message 'Short argument: value', and any other type throws new Exception with message 'Unknown type: type'.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated tokens: type and value.

Output Format:
For num: 'Parsed: v' on success, 'Number problem: bad number' on a parse failure. For arg: 'Argument problem: Short argument: value' when it is shorter than 3 characters, otherwise 'Arg ok: value'. For any other type: 'General problem: Unknown type: type'.

Constraints:
Each token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Checked Unchecked Classifier
questions.description:
The compiler treats the two exception families differently: IOException is checked, so code that can raise it must catch or declare it, while NullPointerException is unchecked and carries no such requirement. Read a mode token. For mode 'checked' raise new IOException with message 'File missing'; for any other mode raise new NullPointerException with message 'Null trouble'. Give each type its own catch block and label the category.

Input Format:
A single token: checked or unchecked.

Output Format:
'Checked caught: File missing' for mode checked. 'Unchecked caught: Null trouble' for any other mode.

Constraints:
The mode token has length between 1 and 20.

questions.title: Banking Ledger Processor
questions.description:
A bank's nightly ledger replays transactions and must survive failures. Define two custom CHECKED exception classes, InsufficientFundsException and NegativeAmountException, both extending Exception with super(message). Read an initial balance, then process n operations: DEPOSIT x adds x (negative x raises NegativeAmountException with message 'Negative amount: x'), WITHDRAW x subtracts x (negative x raises NegativeAmountException; x above the balance raises InsufficientFundsException with message 'Insufficient funds: x'), and BALANCE prints the current balance. Each failed operation is caught, counted and reported, and the ledger keeps processing afterwards. At the end print the final balance and the number of failed operations.

Input Format:
First line: n and the initial balance. Each of the next n lines: an operation — 'DEPOSIT x', 'WITHDRAW x', or 'BALANCE'.

Output Format:
Per operation print 'Deposited: x', 'Withdrawn: x' or 'Balance: b'; for a caught failure print 'Rejected: message' instead. Then print two final lines: 'Final balance: b' and 'Failed operations: f'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= initial balance <= 1000000000, -1000000000 <= x <= 1000000000

questions.title: Batch Jobs with Guaranteed Cleanup
questions.description:
A CI runner executes n jobs one after another, and every job must release its resources — even when it fails mid-run. For each job line (name code): inside try print 'Open name' and, when code is negative, throw new IllegalArgumentException with message 'Bad code: code'; otherwise print 'Run name'. The catch prints 'Error in name: Bad code: code' and counts the failure, while the finally block ALWAYS prints 'Close name'. After all jobs print the success and failure counts.

Input Format:
First line: n. Each of the next n lines: a job name (no spaces) and an integer code.

Output Format:
Per job, in order: 'Open name', then 'Run name' or 'Error in name: Bad code: code', then 'Close name'. Final two lines: 'Successful jobs: s' and 'Failed jobs: f'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000, job name length 1 <= len <= 30, -1000 <= code <= 1000

questions.title: Exception Cause Chain
questions.description:
When a low-level failure travels upward, well-written code wraps it in a higher-level exception while keeping the original as the cause. Read two integers a and b. Method compute(a, b) divides a by b inside its own try; when b is zero it catches the ArithmeticException and rethrows new IllegalStateException('Computation failed for inputs a and b', e) with the original attached as the cause. main catches the IllegalStateException and prints both the wrapper message and the cause's message obtained with getCause().getMessage().

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated integers a and b.

Output Format:
On success: 'Result: q'. On failure: two lines — 'Error: Computation failed for inputs a and b' and 'Caused by: / by zero'.

Constraints:
-1000000 <= a, b <= 1000000
questions.sampleoutput2:
Error: Computation failed for inputs 10 and 0
Caused by: / by zero
questions.output3:
Error: Computation failed for inputs 100 and 0
Caused by: / by zero

questions.title: Mixed Batch Parser
questions.description:
A data-import service receives a batch of tokens: some are integers, some are garbage. NumberFormatException is unchecked — it can surface from Integer.parseInt without any throws declaration, and any parse failure (bad characters OR a value beyond int range) raises it. Read n tokens; try to parse each one as an int; accumulate the sum of the valid ones and count every NumberFormatException. Report both tallies and the total.

Input Format:
First line: n. Second line: n space-separated tokens, each either a 32-bit integer or a non-numeric word.

Output Format:
Three lines: 'Valid entries: v', 'Invalid entries: f' and 'Total sum: s'.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000 and each token has length between 1 and 12

Valid entries: 3
Invalid entries: 2
Total sum: 25

Valid entries: 2
Invalid entries: 1
Total sum: 3000000000

Invalid entries: 0
Total sum: 42
